scope: S2: the session core on Linux x86-64; session rows are Linux only, the Mac runs only what needs no Linux process

rulings.R-sn02-1: finish prints 'Run till exit from #0 ...' and continue prints 'Continuing.' only in gdb's terminal mode; sniff has a small terminal mode (--tty), held to pty transcripts; the prompt and the 80-column wrap are normalised by name
rulings.R-sn02-2: S2 session rows run -O0 C and wolf; -O2 C stays reader-corpus only
rulings.R-sn02-3: ptrace request numbers, user_regs_struct layout and the wait-status truth table come from a compiled C probe run in the oracle container (tools/abi-probe.c, its output committed), never from header text; man pages are the semantics source

exited|killed|signaled.other execution command: refused: The program is not being run.

state_machine.stop_signals: a non-SIGTRAP stop reports 'Program received signal NAME, Description.' and the next resume delivers it; SIGTRAP not from a sniff breakpoint or step is delivered to the inferior (its own handler), not swallowed

ptrace_requests: PTRACE_PEEKUSER (only if GETREGS is not enough)
other_calls: personality(ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE) in the child before exec

wait_statuses.stopped: low byte 0x7f, signal in bits 8-15; the stop at exec is 0x57f
wait_statuses.exited: low 7 bits zero, code in bits 8-15
wait_statuses.signaled: low 7 bits the signal, bit 7 the core flag

output_shapes.run_exit_nonzero: [Inferior 1 (process N) exited with code OO]  (code printed in octal, two digits minimum)
output_shapes.signal_stop:
Program received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
0xADDR in main (argc=2, argv=0xADDR) at FILE:LINE
LINE	SOURCE
output_shapes.signal_death: \nProgram terminated with signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.\nThe program no longer exists.
output_shapes.break_set: Breakpoint N at 0xADDR: file FILE, line L.
output_shapes.info_breakpoints: Num     Type           Disp Enb Address            What / one row per location / '\tbreakpoint already hit N time(s)'; empty: 'No breakpoints, watchpoints, tracepoints, or catchpoints.'
output_shapes.bt: #0  FUNC (ARGS) at FILE:LINE / #N  0xADDR in FUNC (ARGS) at FILE:LINE
output_shapes.finish: Run till exit from #0 ... (terminal mode only), then '0xADDR in CALLER (...) at FILE:LINE\nLINE\tSOURCE\nValue returned is $N = VALUE'
output_shapes.print: $N = VALUE (history numbering); char as '65 'A''; bool true/false; float %.9g; double %.17g; pointer as '(int *) 0xADDR' at top level
output_shapes.info_registers: name, hex value padded to 19, natural value; eflags as [ ZF PF ] flag lists; segment registers decimal

refusals.no_process_execution: The program is not being run.
refusals.no_process_registers: The program has no registers now.
refusals.stripped: No symbol table is loaded.  Use the "file" command.  (symbolic commands only; *ADDRESS still works)
refusals.unmapped_address: Cannot insert breakpoint N.\nCannot access memory at address 0xADDR
refusals.fork_follows_parent_only: sniff states: S2 follows the parent only; the child runs untraced
refusals.script_abort: an error in a -x style script aborts the rest of the script, as gdb does

findings_from_gdb_15_1: Run till exit and Continuing. only in terminal mode
break main in a wolf program makes two locations (module main and the C shim)
next over the program's own int3 trips an internal assert in gdb 15.1: no row is held to that path
batch mode auto-answers queries; pty sessions start gdb with -iex 'set confirm off' and 'set pagination off'

normalisations.load_base: none: both debuggers disable ASLR; PIE base 0x555555554000 must match unnormalised
normalisations.stack_addresses: env and auxv differ between debuggers (LINES/COLUMNS set by gdb); a stack pointer value is normalised by name only on rows that print one, otherwise argv-style values are held exactly under a fixed env
normalisations.thread_db_banner: the two '[Thread debugging using libthread_db enabled]' lines are dropped by name
normalisations.version_banner: gdb's own banner is never produced; sniff prints none
normalisations.pty_prompt: '(gdb) ' / '(sniff) ' prompt and echoed input, tty rows only
normalisations.wrap_80: terminal rows: gdb's 80-column wrap is removed by name
normalisations.lane_root: the configured root prefix of source paths

inferior: c/exits: exit 0, exit 3, exit 255, SIGSEGV, kill while stopped
breakpoints: c/calls: function, file:line, *address, info breakpoints, delete, hit counts
c/hits: several breakpoints at one address, break at current pc then continue, 10000-hit loop
stepping: c/calls: step into function, step over no-line-info plain.c, next over a call, finish, until, stepping off the end of main
wolf/recursion: next stays in frame, finish out of recursion
frames: c/calls and wolf/recursion: bt, frame N, up, down; CFI for C, named frame-pointer fallback for wolf where it has no FDE
values: c/values: print and info locals/args for char, unsigned, short, long, float, double, bool, pointer; finish Value returned for each
wolf/recursion and wolf/hits: locals equal lupin's values at the same source point
hostile: c/signals: program installing its own SIGTRAP handler
stripped binary: symbolic commands refused, *ADDR works
measured: startup to first breakpoint and 10000-hit loop, sniff vs gdb 15.1 interleaved, ratio with stated margin

known_limits_predicted: wolf emits no CFI for its own functions today (s283): wolf bt uses the frame-pointer fallback and the note says which rows
wolf u8/u64/uint carry signed encodings (R-sn00-1): sniff prints what DWARF says and the row names the gap
wolf aggregates are undescribed: print refuses by name, never invents from source
the session layer is Linux x86-64 only; macOS rows compile-check the platform-neutral modules
honesty: A SKIP is never a measurement. A row that did not run is reported as not run.
